content: This information does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. It is not intended to replace individualized medical advice and should not substitute for the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically once daily. For children, it may be prescribed to be taken twice daily (every 12 hours). The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. To achieve the best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, gas, headache, or dizziness. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections). Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking cefixime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefixime may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). The chewable form of this medication may contain aspartame. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., some diabetic urine tests), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not ensure that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
